text: - Project Management Page 16 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric Task 5 provided the project-management structure necessary to coordinate technical activities, maintain schedule discipline, and ensure the quality and completeness of all Budget Period 1 (BP1) deliverables. Consistent with the management framework defined in the Statement of Project Objectives (SOPO), this task oversaw day-to-day execution of modeling, engineering, and analysis activities while ensuring alignment across PGE, GE Vernova, BPA, PNNL, UT Austin, and NextEra Energy. The project management function served as the central point of integration for all work performed under Tasks 1–4 and ensured that BP1 technical goals were completed on time, within scope, and in accordance with DOE requirements. Project oversight was carried out through structured coordination mechanisms that included weekly technical progress meetings, monthly cross-partner alignment discussions, and routine document-sharing and version-control processes. These forums ensured that insights from EMT studies, performance-metric development, plant-level engineering reviews, and HIL testbed development were shared promptly among teams, and that assumptions remained consistent across all modeling and engineering activities. As required by the SOPO, PGE, as the lead institution, maintained responsibility for overall technical direction, partner coordination, and integration of contributions from each organization involved in the project. This role included managing technical risks, tracking action items, validating partner deliverables, and ensuring that the project progressed according to the BP1 baseline schedule. A key component of project management in BP1 was formal tracking of milestones and deliverables. The project team used a structured review workflow that included milestone verification, internal QA checks, and DOE-required reporting through quarterly RPPR submissions. The Q8 RPPR confirmed that all BP1 milestones were completed or appropriately documented within the period of performance, including performance-metric definition, EMT model development, hybrid-plant simulation, FMEA completion, preliminary tuning methodology, and engineering preparation for future commissioning. These deliverables formed the basis for assessing technical readiness and ensuring alignment between BP1 outputs and the subsequent demonstration-focused activities originally planned for BP2. Project management activities also included maintaining compliance with DOE reporting, documentation, and communication requirements. This involved coordination of quarterly reports, participation in DOE technical discussions, maintenance of project records, and centralized tracking of modeling files, engineering notes, and technical documentation referenced throughout BP1. As the project involved national laboratory, OEM, and utility partners, this centralized management structure was essential for ensuring transparency and consistency across all technical contributions. The project team also evaluated schedule risk and dependency management throughout BP1. Coordination across large-scale modeling activities, engineering Page 17 of 36 Award Number: DE-EE0010651 Recipient Name: Portland General Electric reviews, and testbed development required active identification of cross-task dependencies, such as the need to finalize performance metrics before beginning plant-level EMT validation, or completing model-integration activities before HIL synchronization testing. The management structure ensured that these dependencies were addressed proactively and that critical-path tasks remained on schedule. Although DOE subsequently discontinued BP2, the project management work completed in BP1 ensured that all technical outputs were complete, documented, and ready for transition into field-demonstration planning.
